Observed limitation: rank96 native repeats AUC0.6675003890552496 but its first-affine context factors still use29184 weights versus21504 for one dense context map. The latest rank96 native/fused comparison took26.2944/27.5474 inference seconds and15.1634/15.1837ms p50; rank112 native/fused took26.9521/27.4979 seconds and15.0185/15.0416ms p50. Thus fusion has no measured cost benefit here, and rank96 is not already proven faster than112. Rank70 scored0.6668936333381517 while full112 balanced scored0.6674485580556159; the untested80/88 interval is consequential.
study.hypothesis: A small part of the factorized buy-owned context capacity between ranks80 and96 may be removable without losing the shared context signal that supports click prediction. Keep112 nonlinear output channels and semantic target/pool branches intact. Balanced factors may retain more useful optimization dynamics than output-heavy factors at the same rank. This is a bounded extension of an existing mechanism, not a new architecture or novelty claim. Fresh-weight SVD directions are not trained importance estimates. The latest fusion failure motivates fixing native execution, not assuming further rank reduction will be fast. This is a stricter local continuation gate, never permission to relax an earlier frozen criterion. If an earlier applicable criterion is stricter, it also applies. No passing result is yet observed; one seed only permits provisional screening. Call a candidate provisionally useful only if it passes quality, has fewer measured trainable Parameters than the rank96 control, model-only batch p50 latency <=0.99 times the contemporaneous control, p95 <=1.01 times control, and full-validation inference wall time <=1.01 times control. Same device, batch8192, precision, loader and host timing boundaries; include constructor SVD in total wall cost and all executed forward operations in inference timing.
